query: For high-entropy alloys intended as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components, what single intervention could improve heat-transfer capability while preserving structural integrity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the expected outcome compared with current intermediate-layer performance, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing ~5 at.% Ag into an equiatomic TaNbWMo high-entropy alloy intermediate layer will form a percolating network of Ag-rich precipitates that raises thermal conductivity by ≥15% at 600–800 °C while reducing yield strength by ≤10%.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic TaNbWMo refractory HEA intermediate layer, homogenized, grain size ~10 μm, without secondary phases.
generation.intervention: Alloying with 5 at.% silver and aging at 500 °C for 4 h to precipitate Ag-rich particles along grain boundaries.
generation.conditions: Steady‐state exposure at 600–800 °C under cyclic mechanical loads up to 10 MPa in inert gas relevant to plasma‐facing reactor environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Interconnected Ag-rich precipitate network along grain boundaries and triple junctions.
generation.mechanism: High intrinsic thermal conductivity of Ag precipitates provides continuous percolation paths for phonon and electron heat transport, while coherent interfaces maintain load transfer.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity increases from ~15 W/m·K to ≥17.3 W/m·K (≥15% gain) at 600 °C; room‐temperature 0.2% proof stress decreases by ≤10% relative to baseline.
generation.baseline: Current TaNbWMo HEA intermediate layer: k ≈15 W/m·K at 600 °C, 0.2% proof stress ~600 MPa at room temperature.
generation.boundary: Applies to layers aged under 500 °C for 4 h; holds under inert atmosphere, 600–800 °C, cyclic loading ≤10 MPa. Not validated outside this aging regime or under neutron irradiation.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: potential Ag coarsening at high temperature could reduce network connectivity over extended service times.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two TaNbWMo HEA samples: one with 5 at.% Ag and one without. Age both at 500 °C for 4 h. Subject both to 600 °C thermal soak and cyclic 10 MPa loading in inert gas for 100 h. Measure thermal conductivity and room‐temperature 0.2% proof stress.
measurements: Microstructural imaging of Ag precipitate distribution (SEM/EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ag-alloyed sample shows <5% increase in thermal conductivity at 600 °C or >15% reduction in 0.2% proof stress, then the hypothesis is falsified.
